clue.text: Topless American dad on American creation

indicators.note: a topless word has lost its head, so the first letter of the dad's name goes

parts.note: Pop is an American word for father
US is short for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a shirtless American father lounging on a fellow American.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary work, something an artist has made.

clue.text: Do Bart and Homer play a bit on computer?

indicators.note: the letters are allowed to play about, so the names are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether two Simpsons characters appear in a computer game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' is the anagram signal: DOBART plus HOMER (eleven letters) rearrange into the two-word answer, entered across two lights.
explanation.definitionFit: The main circuit board is a central component inside a computer, so it is literally one bit of the machine.

clue.text: Drunk male — unknown prisoner returned to the empty cell

indicators.note: a drunk person is all over the place, so these letters are jumbled
returned means this pair is read backwards

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown, like x
a con is a convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its insides, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A drunken man and an anonymous prisoner are sent back to an empty jail cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' makes MELA; 'returned' turns the pair round to NOCY. 'Cell' is biological, not a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A melanocyte is a type of skin cell that produces the pigment melanin.

clue.text: Homer's time to gorge

parts.note: to pig is to gorge oneself on food
an eon is a very long period of time

explanation.surface: Homer Simpson deciding it is time for a binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' looks like the Simpson, but here it is a homing bird; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A homer is a homing pigeon, a bird trained to fly back to its loft.

clue.text: Poles protect spy — ask one to leave Russian city

indicators.note: to protect is to wrap round, so the poles enclose the spy

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

indicators.note: to leave means a letter departs from the word ask

parts.note: a is one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Political image of Polish forces shielding an agent, who is told to get out of a Russian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Smolensk is a historic city in western Russia on the Dnieper.

clue.text: Lift Simpson boy's bottom first

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom letter of the name is moved up to the front

parts.note: Bart is the son in The Simpsons

explanation.surface: Someone lifts Bart Simpson bottom first, like a parent picking up a child.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is rotated: its last letter goes to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bar is a type of ski lift that tows skiers uphill.

clue.text: Chops tablet to get fix

parts.note: a cake of soap is a tablet of it
being in a hole is being in a fix, a predicament

explanation.surface: Someone crushes a pill to get their drug fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chops' is a noun meaning the mouth, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for the mouth: chops are the jaws and a cakehole is where food goes.

clue.text: Pop in America lifted flaps

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Americans call fizzy pop soda

explanation.surface: A US pop star hoisted up and getting flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: Ados are fusses, and a flap is a state of agitated fuss.

clue.text: Writing in sounds — The Simpsons frame lost in translation

indicators.note: a translation turns letters into something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the frame of a word is its outer letters, which are lost here

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Simpsons loses its picture when dubbed into another language.
explanation.walkthrough: SIMPSONS without its first and last S leaves IMPSON; with THE that rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetism is phonetic writing, spelling that represents each spoken sound.

clue.text: See 2
School with a sound in 9?

explanation.surface: Asks whether a school with a certain sound appears in phonetic writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 refers to 9 across, phonetic writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The schwa is the neutral unstressed vowel, written as an upturned e in the phonetic alphabet.

clue.text: They blow up both sides — died from grenades exploding

indicators.note: exploding blows the letters apart into a new order

parts.note: L and R are left and right, both sides

indicators.note: from signals the letter being taken away from the word grenades

parts.note: D is short for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Grenades go off on both flanks and someone dies.
explanation.walkthrough: GRENADES loses D to give GRENAES; with L and R those letters are rearranged. 'Blow up' is photographic enlargement, not explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographic enlargers make bigger prints, and to blow up a picture is to enlarge it.

clue.text: Box has repeat of old comic's work?

indicators.note: the box takes in a repeat of the letter for old, so another one goes inside

parts.note: a carton is a box

explanation.surface: The TV box is showing a repeat of an old comedian's show.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon is a drawn comic strip or animated film, the kind of thing a comic artist produces.

clue.text: Puts in Morse lines during Lewis?

indicators.note: during means the lines come within the author's initials

parts.note: C S Lewis was the author of the Narnia books
an ode is a poem, a set of lines

explanation.surface: Detective drama: Morse puts in some lines during an episode of Lewis.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis and Morse both suggest the Oxford TV detectives; here Lewis is the author C S Lewis and Morse is the code.
explanation.definitionFit: To encode a message in Morse is to turn it into dots and dashes, a coding system.

clue.text: Introduction to Krusty — where 21 and 22 across are found turning over channels?

indicators.note: turning over means the whole string is read backwards
the introduction to a word is its opening letter

parts.note: both those entries sit on the tenth row of this grid

explanation.surface: Krusty the Clown flicking between channels, though the grid refers to itself.
explanation.walkthrough: K plus ROWTEN read backwards. Krusty is the clown in The Simpsons.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcasting network is a group of linked channels carrying the same programmes.

clue.text: Winding round quite tightly, primarily restricting vessel with this?

definitions.text: Winding round quite tightly, primarily restricting vessel with this?

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the vessel goes inside
primarily means only the opening letter of tightly is used

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: winding twists the letters around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: Describes binding a cord tightly round a limb to stop the blood in a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winding' scrambles quite into IQUET; 'restricting' puts the vessel between the opening pieces and that scramble. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourniquet is a band wound tight around a limb to restrict a blood vessel and stop bleeding.

clue.text: Ask Apu? Two bottles smashed

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold inside, so the words contain the answer

explanation.surface: At the Kwik-E-Mart, someone asks Apu about two bottles that got smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: Apu is the shopkeeper in The Simpsons. 'bottles' looks like a noun but is a verb meaning holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaput is informal for broken or ruined, so it means smashed.

clue.text: Small job outside Springfield?

indicators.note: outside means the job goes round the small letter

parts.note: a duty is a job or task
S is short for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A minor task on the edge of Springfield, the town in The Simpsons.
explanation.walkthrough: Springfield suggests the Simpsons' town, but it is the 1960s British singer Dusty Springfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty Springfield was a famous British pop singer, so Dusty is an example of a Springfield.

clue.text: TV animation artist close to pen

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the miser holds the artist

parts.note: close can mean mean with money, so stingy
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A cartoon artist is near a pen for drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' is an adjective meaning tight-fisted, and 'pen' is a verb. Stingray was a 1960s British puppet TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingray was a British children's TV show made with puppets, a kind of screen animation.

clue.text: Recall comic rabbit

indicators.note: recall means call back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Peter Kay is a British comedian

explanation.surface: Remembering a cartoon rabbit, perhaps Bugs Bunny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' is a verb in British slang, meaning to chatter on.
explanation.definitionFit: To yak and to rabbit are both slang for talking at length about trivia.

clue.text: Yankee, small child following ring on banks of skate park

indicators.note: following means the child comes after the earlier pieces

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its edges, so the outer letters of skate

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: An American kid trailing round the edge of a skate park.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite is a national park in California famous for its granite cliffs.

clue.text: Need animated film to finish

parts.note: to need something is to have use for it
Up is a 2009 Pixar animated film

explanation.surface: Someone needs a cartoon film to round off the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: To use up something is to finish it, consuming it entirely.

clue.text: We pick off clips to cover TV series

indicators.note: to cover means to wrap round, so the series goes inside

parts.note: snips are clips, as with scissors
ER was a long-running US hospital drama

explanation.surface: Editors cutting clips from a TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Snipers are marksmen who pick off targets from hiding.

clue.text: Homer Simpson's endorsing characters? He wanted to phone home with this?

definitions.text: Homer Simpson's endorsing characters? He wanted to phone home with this?

parts.note: the initial characters of Homer and Simpson, as signed on a cheque, H and S
ET, the film alien, wanted to phone home

explanation.surface: Homer Simpson signing his initials, while E.T. wants something to phone home with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endorsing characters' means initials, as in signing the back of a cheque; written out, H and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A handset is the part of a telephone you hold, which the alien could use to call his planet.

clue.text: A man wise in conversation around daughter on American prime time?

parts.note: he is a man, a male pronoun

indicators.note: around means the two letters go either side
in conversation means the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: the word wise is said aloud like two letter Ys

explanation.surface: A wise man talks around his daughter during American prime-time TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' spoken sounds like 'Ys', two Ys; they go round D on A.
explanation.definitionFit: A heyday is the period when someone or something is at its peak, their prime.

clue.text: Marge, maybe, before wearing down

indicators.note: wearing means being worn inside, so it goes into the other word

parts.note: down means sad, low in spirits
pre is a prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: Marge Simpson is feeling depressed before something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marge' suggests Marge Simpson, but it is British slang for margarine.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is an example of a spread for bread.

clue.text: Thatcher with Home Secretary's number

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher was nicknamed Maggie
Theresa May was Home Secretary when the puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: Political pairing of a former PM and the then Home Secretary's figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a song: Maggie May was a 1971 hit for Rod Stewart.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song or musical piece, and Maggie May is a famous rock song.

clue.text: Mum quiet in TV series

parts.note: Ma is an informal word for mother
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Mother stays silent while watching a TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: M*A*S*H was a long-running American sitcom set in an army hospital in Korea.

clue.text: Man perhaps is on shortly

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: on side is another name for leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone's man is about to come on in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the pitch is also called the on side. 'Man' is the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea, so Man is an example of one.

clue.text: Question published in book

parts.note: a newspaper ran a story, published it

explanation.surface: A question appears in print in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Quran is the holy book of Islam.

clue.text: Armani keen to show designer label

indicators.note: to show means letters are revealed within the words Armani keen

explanation.surface: Armani eager to display its designer label.
explanation.definitionFit: Nike is a sportswear brand whose logo is a famous label.

clue.text: Lisa Simpson's right about slow person

indicators.note: about means moving the letters around

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the right-hand end of the name is its last letter

explanation.surface: Lisa Simpson is right about someone being slow.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the last letter of Simpson, is rearranged with LISA.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail is a sluggish creature, so a slow person can be called one.

clue.text: Custom to record The Simpsons, for example

parts.note: custom is trade, as in a shop's custom
to mark is to record, as when marking down a score

explanation.surface: Arranging a custom recording of The Simpsons.
explanation.definitionFit: The Simpsons name is a registered brand, the legal property of its owners.
